description:
Programme or Project Overview

VU Amsterdam advertises a PhD student position in cellular neuroscience, studying mRNA localization and local protein synthesis in synapse formation, funded by NWO. Neurons localise specific messenger RNAs to synaptic compartments and translate them on site - a process central to how synapses form, mature and adapt. The project investigates the molecular logic of this local transcriptome and its role in circuit development, using neuronal cultures, imaging and molecular-biology methods.

The doctoral candidate joins VU Amsterdam's cellular neuroscience research environment, which combines cell-biological experimentation with advanced microscopy and quantitative analysis, and collaborates within the Amsterdam neuroscience network. The employment is a salaried four-year PhD position under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement with a starting salary of EUR 3,204 per month, and the candidate participates in the faculty's PhD training programme and international conference circuit.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in neuroscience, biology, biomedical sciences or a related field, with hands-on experience in cell culture or molecular methods and an interest in RNA biology and synaptic mechanisms. Applications are submitted through the workingat.vu.nl portal with CV, transcripts and references; the closing date should be confirmed on the official vacancy page.

Highlights

  • NWO-funded PhD on mRNA localization in synapses
  • Local protein synthesis and circuit development
  • Cell culture, imaging and molecular methods
  • Salaried four-year position (EUR 3,204 - 4,051 per month)
  • Amsterdam neuroscience network participation
  • Closing date - confirm on the official VU page
